_nesting_note: THE SUBFORM PREFIX IS NOT A SECTION. Page 1's fourteen scalars sit at three different depths under F433-B-OIC_Page1[0]: five are its DIRECT children (Business_Name, EIN, County_Business_Location, Description_Business_DBA, Mailing_Address), four are under Col1a[0], three under Col1b[0] (one of those two levels deep, under EmployeesNumber[0]), and one under Col2b[0]. Business_Address is in Col1a and County_Business_Location - printed on the SAME ROW, 7pt apart - is not in any Col subform at all. So no prefix generalises to a section, a column or a row, and none was used to justify a binding. This is the shape recorded on 433-A as "AcroForm nesting depth is not uniform": cells between two sub-tables are siblings of both.

checkboxes._C1_01_TO_C1_04_ARE_TWO_QUESTIONS_AND_NO: THE TRAP ON THIS PAGE. The four leaf names run C1_01, C1_02, C1_03, C1_04 in one unbroken sequence and read exactly like a single four-option group. They are two independent Yes/No pairs on two unrelated questions, and THE INDEX ORDER IS NOT THE PRINTED ORDER: C1_03 and C1_04 (payroll outsourcing) are drawn at y 432.4, ABOVE C1_01 and C1_02 (federal contractor) at y 414.9, and in a different column - x 313.4/353.0 against x 36.0/79.2. Reading the sequence as one set would produce a four-way exclusive rule that no printed question asks, and it would be wrong in both directions at once: it would forbid a business from being a federal contractor AND outsourcing its payroll, which the form plainly allows. Established from the rectangles, not from the names. This is the 433-B(OIC) instance of the recorded shape that AcroForm slot order is not printed order.

Every one of this page's 43 fields is business data a record can supply - there is no signature block, no preparer-use box and no IRS-use cell anywhere on page 1. Checked against the enumeration: all 43 widgets are bound above. 433-A(OIC) declares 5 never-autofill fields and 433-A declares 14, so an empty block here would otherwise read as a step someone forgot.

There is no total-shaped cell on this page at all - no lettered Box, no "Add lines" instruction, no arithmetic of any kind. s1_average_gross_monthly_payroll is the only money cell and it is an INPUT, not a total: nothing on the page adds anything to produce it. So there is nothing for a tripwire to check and nothing to declare not checkable, and the two states are distinguished rather than collapsed.

_partition._why: Declared as the map is authored, not assembled in a closing pass. 433-F accumulated 63 silently unreferenced fields precisely because that declaration was left to the end.
_partition._check: 43 + 0 + 0 = 43 — bound writable, never-autofill, deferred, and their sum is every unique target this map references, which is every field on page 1. Then 267 - 43 = 224 unaccounted: the fields on pages 2 through 6 that this slice has not read. page-geometry reports 43 for p1, 61 for p2, 69 for p3, 30 for p4, 33 for p5 and 31 for p6. EVERY FIGURE IN THIS BLOCK IS DERIVED AND RE-DERIVED ON EVERY GATE RUN by adapters/pdf/count-sweep.mjs [S-01, S-02, S-03] against the field list and the widget geometry; none is typed.
_partition._why_unaccounted_is_the_word_and_not_def: A FIRST DRAFT OF THIS BLOCK CALLED PAGES 2-6 `deferred` AND THE COUNT SWEEP REFUSED IT. The two words are not synonyms in this engine and the distinction is the point. `deferred` is derived by classifyMapTargets from fields the map NAMES under a `_deferred` key — an enumerated list of specific cells this slice declines to bind. `unaccounted` is derived from widget geometry over pages the map has not authored at all. Pages 2 to 6 are not a list of deferred cells; they are pages nobody has read yet, and calling them deferred would be a glob claiming the granularity of an enumeration. Slice 1 has read one page and says so. This map is therefore NOT CLOSED, which is worth stating because the other three maps in this repo all say THE MAP IS CLOSED and a reader who skims will expect it here; the figure falls to zero when slice 4 lands and not before.

_arguable_page1.what: The printed cell is 18.0pt wide (x 126.0..144.0) and carries no /MaxLen.
_arguable_page1.why_it_is_arguable: 18pt of the form's body face holds roughly two digits, maybe three. A business with 1,200 employees has a true answer this cell cannot print, and the PDF declares no /MaxLen for the fill engine to refuse against - so a four-digit value would be written, silently overflow the rectangle, and print clipped or not at all. Every other narrow cell on the three mapped forms that has this problem declares a /MaxLen; this one does not.
_arguable_page1.what_this_slice_did: Bound it, and recorded the width. NOT resolved: whether the engine should impose a ceiling the PDF does not declare is a question about diverging from the form, and this repo's standing position is that the form is the authority.

_arguable_page1.what: One printed cell carries two facts - the description of the business AND the DBA or trade name.
_arguable_page1.why_it_is_arguable: The caption is "Description of business and DBA or "Trade Name"" over a single widget. A CRM holding those as two properties must join them to fill this cell, and the join order is not printed. The same shape occurs at partners.percent_ownership_and_annual_salary, which pairs a percentage with a salary in one cell.
_arguable_page1.what_this_slice_did: Bound the cell as one key and declared the two-facts-one-cell shape in the row-shape spec for the partner column. NOT resolved: the crosswalk decides whether the backbone holds one property or two, and that is slice 5.

NOT resolved: whether the entity type should be captured as data at all is a product question, not a mapping one.

s1_total_number_of_employees is an 18.0pt cell with NO /MaxLen. A four-digit headcount would be accepted by the PDF and drawn clipped or not at all, and no declared limit exists for the fill engine to refuse against.

Two printed cells each carry two facts: s1_description_of_business_and_dba, and the partner column percent_ownership_and_annual_salary. Whether the backbone holds one property or two is a crosswalk decision, not a mapping one.
The four eligibility bullets read like an entity-type selector and have NO widget against them. Recorded with the evidence so a later slice does not go looking for four missing checkboxes.

DECLARATION COVERAGE DOES NOT RUN ON THIS FORM. The coverage table - including the row_class kind added for ruling 5 - is built inside gate step 11, and step 11 SKIPS when a form has no totals file. 433-B(OIC) page 1 prints no total, so it correctly has none, and the consequence is that this map's one row_class declaration is counted by nothing: the gate reports declarations_total n/a. The declaration is not thereby unchecked - its refusal path is proved by adapters/pdf/assert-row-class-routes.mjs and its acceptance path by adapters/pdf/check-row-shape.mjs, which reported 3 slotted rows across 1 declaring group on this slice's fill - but it is absent from the table that exists to NAME unexercised declarations, which is the gap ruling 5 was written about, one level out. Moving the coverage table out of step 11 is a refactor of a guard, and its no-op path would have to be proved on the three finished forms in the same run. Not attempted in this slice.
